title: Multicolour Ramsey number R_4(3) = R(3,3,3,3), lower bound
statement: Find a colouring of the edges of K_n with 4 colours 0..3 in which colour c holds no complete graph K_(S_(c+1)), for (S_1, ..., S_4) = (3,3,3,3); it shows R(3,3,3,3) > n. The best known lower bound is R(3,3,3,3) >= 51, so a colouring of K_50 is known and one of K_51 or more would improve it.
submission: Text file: the n x n colour matrix, one line of n characters per vertex; the character in row i, column j (i != j) is the colour of the edge {i,j}, a digit from 0 to r-1 (colour c must avoid K_(S_(c+1))), symmetric; diagonal characters are ignored (write 0 or -). n <= 2048 is practical.
score: n, the number of vertices of the colouring; it proves R(3,3,3,3) >= n + 1 (larger is better)

best_known.source: R(3,3,3,3) >= 51: [Chu1] in Small Ramsey Numbers rev. 18 (24 Apr 2026), Table XIa; read 8 Nov 2026

provenance.keeper: Small Ramsey Numbers (S. Radziszowski), EJC Dynamic Survey DS1
